hook.text: She linked Note A to Note B. Months later, when reading Note B, the backlink to Note A surfaced a forgotten connection.

buildup.text: Bidirectional links mean if A links to B, then B automatically links back to A. No connection is ever one-way.

discovery.text: Backlinks surface unexpected relationships. You see which ideas cluster together without manually maintaining a table.

twist.text: Too many links create noise. Link only when a meaningful connection exists, not just because two notes share a keyword.

climax.text: When linking, ask: does knowing about A genuinely change how I think about B? If yes, link. If not, skip.

punchline.text: Link with intention. Meaningful connections beat keyword matches.

quiz.question: When should you create a bidirectional link between two notes?
options: Whenever two notes contain the same keyword
When knowing about one genuinely changes how you think about the other
Only when both notes are about the same topic
